newsitem.title: USA: U.S. September S&Ps end up, recoup Monday's losses.
newsitem.headline: U.S. September S&Ps end up, recoup Monday's losses.

text.p: U.S. September Standard & Poor's 500 futures finished sharply higher, recouping the bulk of Monday's losses on signs the U.S. economy was in good shape in the second quarter, traders and floor analysts said.
U.S. June consumer confidence rose more than expected to its highest level in 28 years. Ken Goldstein, senior economist at the Conference Board, said confidence could rise further.

However, not only was the selloff in T-bonds limited, but cash Treasuries ended the day modestly higher. September T-bonds finished flat. Stock index futures traders said bonds' reaction solidified ideas that U.S. rates would remain low.

Goldstein also said he expected the unemployment rate to fall further to perhaps 4.5 percent from 4.8 percent in May, and said consumer confidence levels indicated that consumers expect employment conditions to remain firm.

However, the U.S. bond market remained resilient in the afternoon and propelled a local short-covering rally in the Standard & Poor's 500 futures pit into a full-fledged buying spree from dealers and funds.
Traders reported heavy arbitrage buy programs at a premium of 9.80 points to cash, and said buy-stop orders were "massive" once September breached 896.00.
Light buy-stops were touched once it rallied through the 894.50 level, which was the contract's daily high for most of the session.

They said portfolio and fund managers were also loading up on U.S. stocks due to quarter-end pressures, and on ideas that consumer confidence could lead to consumer spending which would bolster some corporate earnings.

In addition, San Francisco Federal Reserve President Robert Parry said he saw no clear sign of an end to the U.S. economic recovery that started in April 1991. He said he currently saw robust growth and well-behaved inflation.
After the market closed, Parry said he was a little surprised by the sharp jump in June consumer confidence and said he did not believe the U.S. economy had entered a new era.
U.S. May durable goods and existing home sales will be released on Wednesday morning.
Fair value for September is at 8.40 to 8.60 points over cash, with arbitrage sell programs at a premium of 7.00 points, floor traders said.

At the end of pit trade, September S&Ps were up 23.25 at 905.00, KCBT Value Lines were up 11.25 at 795.50, NYSE Composites were 10.50 higher at 470.80, Nikkeis rose 210 to 20,430, Midcap 400s were up 3.25 at 291.80, and Russell 2000s were 3.60 higher at 398.25. ((Derivatives desk 312-408-8750))
